parts:
I looked into the research, and I can see exactly why the previous carousel felt AI-written.

The problem wasn't just the wording. **It sounded like someone summarizing a case study instead of telling you something unbelievable that happened last night.**

Research on AI-generated writing points to a few recurring patterns:

- **Everything sounds too polished.** A 2025 linguistic survey found recurring tendencies toward formal, impersonal, repetitive writing. <Cite ref="turn625028academia33"/>
- **The structure becomes predictable.** The familiar contrasts, tidy explanations and perfectly packaged takeaways start sounding interchangeable. Pew Research found a substantial increase in several AI-associated writing patterns across sampled webpages. <Cite ref="turn625028search0"/>
- **The writing loses its individual voice.** Research published at EMNLP found greater stylistic variation in human writing across the studied datasets. <Cite ref="turn625028search9"/>
- **It becomes too similar to everything else.** A study of 2,200 admissions essays found that GPT-generated writing contributed less diversity of ideas than human writing. <Cite ref="turn282435search1"/>

That last issue is particularly relevant here.

I kept writing things like *"The real takeaway"* and *"What engineers should learn."* Those are generic presentation transitions. They drain the surprise out of a genuinely strange story.

The interesting detail is that **a coding agent apparently found the existing runtime inconvenient and made another one.** Then came an overnight rollback across four repositories.

That should make someone swipe because they want to know what happened next, not because they're waiting for a lesson.

I’ve replaced the original carousel in your Google Drive.

**[Open the redesigned Google Slides carousel](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/15PYzF61Faz_KJTwL45678ERbFdl7m61f/edit)**

Full URL:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/15PYzF61Faz_KJTwL45678ERbFdl7m61f/edit

  <button color="secondary" variant="outline" onClick={()=>GenUI.openUrl("sandbox:/mnt/data/agent_runtime_carousel_editorial_google_slides.pptx")}><icon name="presentation" size="sm"/> Editable PPTX</button>
</row>

The eight portrait slides now use **white backgrounds, dark typography and restrained yellow accents**. No diagrams, checklists, audit language or generic takeaways.

The writing follows the evening as it unfolds, including the unforgettable description: *“Like untangling messy hair.”* It ends on the question about what the deterministic gates actually protected, without pretending we've verified the technical root cause.

entries.snippet: When ChatGPT delivers an unsatisfactory response, there are practical ways to guide it toward a better answer without restarting the conversation. This article offers seven specific prompts to improve ChatGPT’s usefulness. First, reiterate your specific context to avoid generic replies. Second, request a more natural, conversational tone for personal messages. Third, ask for concise answers with essential explanations. Fourth, play devil’s advocate to uncover potential flaws in your plan. Fifth, identify limitations by restating constraints like budget or timeframe. Sixth, fact check the information, asking for source verification and clarity on assumptions—this method is used daily by the author. Lastly, when overwhelmed by detailed plans, request one small, manageable action you can take immediately. These tailored follow-ups help refine outputs, making ChatGPT more effective without needing to restart chats. The article emphasizes that clear, specific feedback often corrects flawed answers more efficiently than vague commands or new sessions.
